hero.title: Three Wwise Projects
hero.lead: Three school projects where I learned Wwise by running into real problems and figuring out how to fix them. Managing sound limits in a zombie shooter. Making audio adapt between game zones without cuts. Fitting everything into 15 MB on Android.
hero.context: Solo school projects from DAE (2021-2024). Not shipped games, but I treated them like real work - tracking memory, hitting platform limits, writing integration code.

section.title: The Projects
section.subtitle: Three different problems that made me learn how audio middleware actually works under the hood.

boney.title: Boney Boogaloo
boney.p1: Wave shooter with zombies. Max 5 on screen at once. This was my first time using Wwise.
boney.p2: Kept hitting the 256 voice limit because the player shoots constantly and zombies keep spawning. Made random containers with 6 different gunshot sounds and 6 spawn sounds so it doesn't get repetitive.
boney.p3: Spent time balancing volumes in Wwise - shots at -2dB, player hurt at +4dB, zombies at -5dB. Cut silence from the files and used ADPCM compression.
boney.p4: 44 sounds across 9 random containers. Everything goes straight to Master Bus, no effects, all 2D.
boney.video_caption: Every gunshot sounds different. Up to 5 zombies on screen.

ellen.title: Ellen
ellen.p1: Platformer with magic combat. My first attempt at spatial audio.
ellen.p2: Made 10 attenuation curves - enemies heard from 25m, footsteps from 75m, explosions from 100m. Footsteps change based on surface type using raycasts.
ellen.p3: Ambient sound changes between zones using State groups - layers crossfade over 6.5 seconds when you move around. Made 4 reverb buses for different room sizes.
ellen.p4: Compression: Music Q8 OGG, Ambience Q7, SFX Q5, voice ADPCM.
ellen.video_caption: Spatial audio with dynamic reverb and material switching.

stomach.title: Stomach Aches
stomach.p1: FPS platformer set inside a human body. Three zones - Brain, Mouth, Stomach. Had to make it run on cheap Android phones with 2GB RAM.
stomach.p2: Android audio budget was 15MB total. Made zone-based loading so only the current zone's sounds are in memory. Brain 670KB, Mouth 384KB, Stomach 2.8MB.
stomach.p3: Used Wwise's Silence plugin instead of actual silent files - saved 80% memory. The waterfall has 3 layers that blend based on how close you are: Close 130KB, Mid 6.3MB, Far 3.6MB using RTPC.
stomach.p4: Footsteps switch materials. Music streams from disk to save RAM. Had to clean up loops properly so sounds don't get stuck playing.
stomach.video_caption: Waterfall layers blend as you approach. Zone-based loading keeps memory under 15MB.

learned.title: What I Learned
learned.subtitle: Skills from fixing problems when they broke
learned.skill1_desc: Working within sound channel limits, tracking memory budgets, picking compression that balances file size vs quality.
learned.skill2_desc: Writing distance curves for different sound types, positioning audio in 3D space, making sounds fade at the right ranges.
learned.skill3_desc: Connecting game events to middleware, making audio respond to player position and game state without hardcoding values.
learned.skill4_desc: Deciding what loads immediately, what streams from disk, what unloads when changing zones. Staying under budget on phones.
learned.skill5_desc: Writing C# scripts that talk to Wwise API, handling zone triggers, cleaning up sounds that don't stop properly.
learned.skill6_desc: Different compression strategies for PC vs mobile. Testing on emulators. Profiling memory to catch issues before shipping.
